newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mostly higher, July up on China.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mostly higher, July up on China.

text.p: CBOT soybeans ended mostly higher Thursday, as talk of Chinese interest in U.S. soybeans and ideas that supplies continue tight, rallied nearby futures, traders and analysts said.

"The commercial buying we've seen is tied to the need to find some beans," said Jack Scoville, analyst with The Price Group brokerage. "These guys need beans otherwise Cargill wouldn't be importing five cargos from Brazil."
On Wednesday, Cargill Inc said tight supplies of U.S. soybeans had forced the company to contract for an unspecified quantity of Brazilian soybeans.

The late boost in futures Thursday was also spurred in part by rumors of Chinese interest in U.S. and Brazilian soy. However, exporters and traders in both countries were unable to offer confirmation of any trades.
Brazilian soybeans still hold a discount to those in the U.S., which makes large Chinese purchases of U.S. soybeans unlikely, traders and analysts said.
CBOT soybeans settled 3/4 cent per bushel lower to six cents higher, with July up six at $8.36 a bushel.
Old crop contracts labored for most of the day under pressure from export data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture. USDA reported that old crop export sales were a negative 50,700 tonnes.
New crop soybeans sales of 556,200 were more robust and considered supportive to futures, traders said.
Traders also cited technical strength as a reason for the late jump in prices. July soybeans were able to hold $8.25 per bushel, which was seen as key support for that contract, traders said.
"The bears were unable to keep July under $8.25," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "If you get below that, you break the neck line of the head and shoulders (chart formation)."
On the day, Prudential sold six million bushels July, Smith Barney bought five million July, and Cargill bought 3.5 million July, pit traders said.
In options trade, R.J. O'Brien bought 2,300 July $8.00 puts and Griffin Trading sold 2,000 July $8.75 calls.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts. That figure compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 115,581.
